Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/2055: Restriction of Intentionally Added Microplastics

Institutional Document: European Commission Directorate-General for Environment | Published September 28, 2025

Scope of REACH Annex XVII Entry 78

Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/2055 amends Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH) by establishing an EU-wide prohibition on the marketing and placing on the market of synthetic polymer microparticles (SPMs) on their own or in mixtures at concentrations equal to or greater than 0.01% by weight. The regulation targets intentionally added microplastics across cosmetics, detergents, artificial sports turf infill, and controlled-release agricultural chemicals.

The regulatory definition encompasses solid synthetic polymers insoluble in water with all dimensions between 0.1 micrometers and 5 millimeters (or fiber lengths between 0.3 micrometers and 15 millimeters with length-to-diameter ratio > 3).

Transitional Periods and Agricultural Sector Compliance

To enable chemical manufacturers to engineer biodegradable polymeric encapsulants, the regulation provides staggered transition windows. While microbeads in exfoliant rinse-off cosmetics took immediate effect, encapsulants used in plant protection products and controlled-release fertilizers enjoy an 8-year transition period ending in 2031.

Agricultural film mulches and compostable polymers must meet rigorous OECD 301/302 biodegradability criteria, proving at least 90% mineral degradation into water, carbon dioxide, and biomass within 24 months in natural agricultural soils without leaving persistent bioaccumulative residues.
